title: Partitioning and File Management: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Partitioning and File Management: Visual Guide

1. Pruning Two Scales | a 3.65 TB table laid out unpartitioned, by year and by day, with a one-day query shown eliminating bytes at partition level and then at row-group level | partition pruning removes files before any are opened and row-group statistics then prune inside the survivors, so the two mechanisms multiply

2. The Granularity Curve | partition granularity dragged from year to per-user, showing partition count, bytes each, files each and bytes scanned, plus two things that break pruning | finer partitions prune more and cost more to plan, high cardinality wants bucketing rather than one partition per value, and a wrapped column disables pruning entirely

3. Cost Per Object | an 8 GB partition written as objects from 1 MB to 8 GB, showing objects to open, tasks to schedule and available parallelism | the small-file problem is fixed per-object cost rather than bytes, and very large files fail in the other direction by capping parallelism and weakening statistics

4. Swap, Never Mutate | the five-step safe compaction workflow beside the in-place version, ending in a reader that double counts | compaction writes new immutable files and swaps a metadata pointer atomically, so readers see the old set or the new set and never a mixture

5. When Compaction Fails | four failure points classified as before commit, after commit, or conflict, with the recovery each one needs | failure before commit leaves removable orphans, a conflict is detected at commit, and a crash after a confirmed commit must never retry as though the inputs were still active
